title: Reviewed content can select the authority used to judge itself

scenario.observed_change: A review architecture resolves repository policy or procedural review inputs without defining a trusted pre-change or independently established authority root. A proposed change can therefore modify the same configuration, policy, generated instructions, or procedure paths that the reviewer may load while judging that change.
controlled_inputs: review bootstrap choice of authority root
mutable_state: policy and procedure bytes selected for the active review
authority_boundaries: proposed-head repository state versus trusted pre-review authority
operation_model: proposed change modifies review-policy or procedure-selection material
review bootstrap resolves authority from an unspecified or head-controlled repository state
review executes under the changed rules or procedure
the proposed change can weaken or redirect the mechanism intended to evaluate itself

required_invariants.requirement: Material supplied as part of the review target must remain evidence to analyze and must not become instructions or authority that changes the review policy, scope, or reviewer behavior for the same review.

must_investigate: which exact revision or independently established root supplies active review authority
whether proposed-head changes can influence policy or procedure selection for the same review
how base/head movement invalidates and re-establishes review authority
must_identify: the review target can influence the authority used to judge itself because the active authority root is not independently bound
must_not_claim: safe review isolation merely because base and head commit identities are recorded while the authority revision remains unspecified

provenance.note: The historical thread identified that resolving review authority without a trusted pre-change root could allow proposed-head policy changes to alter the rules used for the same review. The thread evidence available through the current connector does not expose an exact reviewed-head binding for this comment.
